about: Unicode text -> Shree-Lipi 7 Tamil bytes (fonts SHREE-TAM7-0800..0803/1316/3883 = S0800890..S0803890/S1316890/S3883890.TTF and Shree-Tam7-001/002 = WTAM7001/2.TTF; the 4/5/6 fonts SHREE-TAM-0800..0803/1316/3883 = S08000F0..S08030F0/S13160F0/S38830F0.TTF have the same code set, identical glyphs except 9B 9F BA = ரி ரீ ர் redrawn), answered by Shree's own composers S8TamU64.dll (TutorGetMappedCodeW, Unicode) and S8Tam764.dll (TutorGetMappedCode, raw bytes) for the same keystroke. bytes = the 7 composer's raw output, one hex byte per glyph code (bytes 80-9F are raw bytes: in a document they sit on their Windows-1252 code points; 80 81 8A 8D 8E 8F 90 9D 9E and every byte under 20 have no glyph). Every probe set and every vendor keyboard was captured twice in separate processes: byte-identical. kind: vendor-key = a key (layer 0, Ctrl+Space, or the composer raw code layer) of one of the 22 shipped .TAM keyboards loaded from its ORIGINAL path (the composers switch typing mode by name); source names the keyboard, key and codes. canonical = probe in Shree's typing order for Tamil (visual order): the pre-base sign first (ெ 76 = F6, ே 62 = F7, ை 75 = F8), then the consonant (each consonant has a block: base, +1 ி, +2 ீ, +3 ு, +4 ூ, +5 ்: க 50 51 52 53 54 55; exceptions ந 7C 7B 7D 7E A1 A2, ம A9 AA AB 95 89 AE, ர B5 9B 9F B8 B9 BA), then the post-base sign (ா 74 = F5 after the letter; ொ = F6 C F5, ோ = F7 C F5, ௌ = F6 C CD); the native ு comes from the precomposed codes 41-59/7E/7F/D5 (கு = 53), the native ூ from code 40 (கூ = 54); on the Grantha letters ஜ ஷ ஸ ஹ ஶ க்ஷ the separate hooks FA/FC (FB/FD on ஷ க்ஷ) from codes 5D/5E; clusters = C1 + pulli 66 (the C1் glyph) + C2 as its own syllable; ஸ்ரீ = FF (code D8) or ஸ் + ரீ = EC 9F; க்ஷ = F1 (code D7) or க் + ஷ = 55 E5. canonical:au = ெ + C + ள filed under C + ௌ (the vendor ௌ keys type exactly this; the Unicode composer misreads it as Cளெ, kept in uComposer). canonical:old-orthography = the pre-1978 ligatures (னா E0, றா D9, ணா 74, the ை curl F9 on ணை லை ளை னை): accepted, ranked after the modern spelling. canonical:secondary = ஷ/க்ஷ + 40 (generic hook FC): accepted, ranked after 5E (FD). canonical:join = round 2 (W probes): two or three syllables typed in one keystroke; the 7 composer wrote the syllables' own answers joined in 21,224 of 21,224 probes, so these rows are filed under the syllables' own Unicode answers joined (the Unicode composer keeps a pre-base sign pending and puts it on the last letter of the keystroke - its answer is kept in uComposer). preferred: a main canonical spelling, then vendor key, then fewer bytes, then more probes; accepted keeps every canonical and vendor spelling. alt:* = the composer answer for a visually non-standard form, kept, not used as truth: the Grantha hook 5D/5E on a native consonant (க + FA), the ை curl D3 on a letter that never took it, an old ligature with a pre-base sign. quirk:* = the Unicode composer wrote something other than the codes mean (a pre-base sign struck after its letter goes on a . carrier; ெ C + ஂ/ஃ/joiner puts ெ after them), or the 7 composer dropped a code the Unicode composer wrote (5F ு, 20 ஂ, A1-A3, A6), a code only the 7 composer types (03 E0 86 80 83 57), not text (two signs, a sign after the pulli or after an independent vowel), Vedic accents, a byte with no glyph in any face (the symbol codes the 7 composer writes under 20: ௶ 09, ௷ 0A, [ ] 0B 0C, “ ” 0D 0E, # $ < > @ _ { } 12-1B, ₹ 1E, | 1C), or a lone vowel sign - kept for evidence, not used. Unicode keys are what the Unicode composer wrote, in NFC (ெ+ா = ொ, ே+ா = ோ, ெ+ௗ = ௌ), except canonical:au as said. Rules with examples: tam7-patterns.txt. Strings a table needs that the composer never spells directly: tam7-composer-gaps.json (derived, not truth).

counts.probeSets: P capp/P-results.json, E capx/E-results.json, W capw/W-results.json

fontCheck.method: fonts/family-check.json (fontcmp.js + ttf.js): (3,1) cmap of every installed Tamil Shree face - 7: WTAM7001/2.TTF (Shree-Tam7-001/002), S0800890..S0803890 + S1316890 + S3883890 (SHREE-TAM7-0800..0803/1316/3883); 4/5/6: S08000F0..S08030F0 + S13160F0 + S38830F0 (SHREE-TAM-0800..0803/1316/3883). Per code: glyph id, advance, sha1 of the glyf bytes.
fontCheck.result: The 12 SHREE-TAM7-xxxx / SHREE-TAM-xxxx faces have the same 213 codes (20-7E except 3C, 82-89, 8B 8C, 91-9C, 9F, A0-FF) on the same code points; same-number pairs are identical in 210 codes and differ ONLY in 9B 9F BA (ரி ரீ ர், redrawn). Shree-Tam7-001/002 add 3C. One table serves both families code for code; the 7 vs 4/5/6 difference is the drawing of ரி ரீ ர் only (same Unicode, same bytes).

glyphCheck.sheets: fonts/all-0800-20-9F.png, fonts/all-0800-A0-FF.png (every code of SHREE-TAM7-0800), fonts/u-forms.png, fonts/old-forms.png, fonts/symbols.png, fonts/ri-rii-r-7-vs-456.png
glyphCheck.rightAsWritten: every consonant block (base, ி, ீ, ு, ூ, ்), ா F5, ெ F6, ே F7, ை F8, the old ை curl F9, the Grantha hooks FA FB FC FD, ஸ்ரீ FF, க்ஷ F1-F4, the old னா E0 / றா D9 / ணா 74, ஃ 4C, । 3E, ‘ ’ 22 27, ÷ 24, — 97, the Tamil number/calendar signs 84 85 98 4D 4E 4F 99 9A FE (shapes consistent, not verified against a reference)

wrongGlyph.ஂ (code 77): 54 = the கூ glyph (no Tamil face has an anusvara): rows filed as quirk, not truth
wrongGlyph.௦-௯ (codes 30-39): bytes 30-39 draw WESTERN digits 0-9 (no Tamil digit glyphs in any face); the Unicode composer writes Tamil digits for these codes
wrongGlyph.॥ (code ED): 88, the same byte as ௳ (E2); no double danda in any face: rows filed as quirk, not truth

counts.wProbes: round 2 (gen-w.js, capw/ + capw-b/ byte-identical): 21,224 keystrokes of two or three syllables (every pair of 13 syllable shapes on 11 letters + 12 vowels; all 24 letters with a pre-base sign before/after a neighbour; 78 common words that fit in 4 codes and 353 syllable pairs/triples from 341 common words). The 7 composer wrote the syllables' own answers joined in 21,224/21,224 (wjoin.json): Tamil syllables join by plain concatenation, no rule reaches across them. The Unicode composer did not in 4,424 (a pre-base sign stays pending and lands on the last letter of the keystroke) - those rows are filed under the syllables' answers joined.
counts.notProbed: A slot holds at most 4 codes, so these are not in the truth as one keystroke: a two-part sign (ொ ோ ௌ = 3 codes) on the second consonant of a cluster (C1 66 ெ C2 ா = 5 codes; C1 66 ெ C2 IS probed, and Tamil clusters are plain syllables: C1் + the C2 syllable, which every probed cluster confirms; the W round confirms syllables join with no cross-syllable effect); clusters of three consonants (C1 66 C2 66 is probed, C3 follows as its own syllable); words longer than 4 codes (their syllable pairs and triples are probed). Tamil has no reph, no nukta and no subjoined forms, so those probe classes do not exist for this script.
